answer_1.quote: We propose PATIENT-Ψ, a novel simulated patient agent that integrates cognitive modeling with LLMs... Trainees converse with the simulated patient, PATIENT-Ψ, to formulate its cognitive model.

answer_2.quote: We also demonstrate that automatic evaluations with LLMs fail to assess the simulated patient fidelity... We evaluate over the 40 conversation histories between the experts and PATIENT-Ψ in our user study. LLM-based evaluators tend to underestimate PATIENT-Ψ's fidelity in favor of GPT-4 baseline.
automatic_metrics: Likert scale ratings (1-5) for fidelity dimensions
Accuracy percentages for cognitive model components

answer_3.quote: We attempt to automatically assess the fidelity and accuracy of PATIENT-Ψ and the baseline using two state-of-the-art LLMs as evaluators: GPT-4 and Llama 3 70B... LLMs are prompted to provide ratings on a 5-point Likert scale assessing the fidelity of how closely the simulated patient resembles real patients.
methods: pairwise evaluation with Likert scale prompts
criteria: fidelity (emotional states, conversational styles, maladaptive cognitions)
accuracy of cognitive model components (automatic thoughts, core beliefs, emotions, etc.)

answer_4.quote: We conducted a thorough user study with 20 mental health experts and 13 trainees... Evaluation results from the experts indicate that: (1) PATIENT-Ψ closely resembles real patients... Experts and trainees prefer using PATIENT-Ψ-TRAINER over a strong GPT-4 baseline.
answer_4.guideline: Participants completed structured surveys after interacting with the simulated patients, rating dimensions on Likert scales and answering comparative questions about fidelity, accuracy, effectiveness, and usability.
